description: Model Context Protocol: an open protocol, based on JSON-RPC 2.0, for exposing tools, resources and prompts to any AI application.
The AI application the user works in. It owns the model, the UI and security policy, and runs one MCP client per server.
Model-controlled capabilities: actions and live queries the model decides to call through `tools/call`.
Application-controlled, read-only context identified by URIs, read with `resources/read`.
User-controlled templates a server offers, typically surfaced as slash commands.
A server asking the host to collect input from the user, such as a confirmation or a missing value.
The two standard transports: a local subprocess talking over stdin/stdout, or HTTP POST to one remote endpoint.
RFC 9728 document an HTTP MCP server publishes to tell clients which authorization server issues its tokens.
Forwarding a client's token to upstream APIs. Forbidden in MCP: servers accept only tokens issued for them and use their own credentials upstream.
